fields.v: Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — automated framework that extracts chains of dependent PRs from git history and the SWE-STEPS dataset; compares coding agents and models across three evaluation settings (Individual PR, Global/conversational, PRD-based) on functional correctness and repository health

fields.v: No named SDD approach. Settings compared: (i) Individual PR (SWE-bench-style baseline, stateless, reset after each PR); (ii) Global Memory configuration (conversational coding: PRs given sequentially, shared context, cascading tests); (iii) PRD configuration (PRD-based coding: all PR requirements concatenated into one Product Requirements Document, planner agent writes PLAN.md before implementation). Agents: OpenHands with CodeAct (main; version not stated); Aider via Aider Python SDK (appendix; version not stated), with an extra 'Local' setting. Models: Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5.2 Chat, Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-5.1 Codex Mini (Gemini 2.5 Flash in some tables)

fields.v: Individual/Global: per PR, search -> localise -> implement -> test feedback, in reflection cycles (max 40 iterations each, 3 cycles per PR); Global keeps state and context across the chain. Framework: mine PRs and metadata -> test-driven validation -> chain construction

fields.v: Tasks: SWE-STEPS Mini (15 tasks/80 PRs) for five models and Lite (50 tasks/276 PRs) for two models. Configurations: three settings x models x two agents (OpenHands main, Aider appendix). Baseline: Individual PR setting (SWE-bench style); human Gold Trace for code health. Held constant: agent architecture and three tools, Docker environment and anti-cheat measures, expected function signatures given, budget (3 reflection cycles of max 40 iterations per PR; PRD pooled 3 x N). Acceptance tests: historical F2P and P2P tests, validated by test-patch/fix-patch runs. Repetitions: not stated (single run). Human intervention: none. No statistical tests

fields.v: Individual PR setting scores higher than Global and PRD on Mini and Lite (totals; not in every repository, e.g. Sonnet 4.5 Conan 8 Individual vs 10 Global): e.g. Sonnet 4.5 66.25% -> 43.75% (Global), Gemini 3 Flash 51.25% -> 31.25% (Mini) and 56.52% -> 36.59% (Lite); authors report up to 20 pp inflation and a 15-25% decrease across LLMs; same trend with Aider. Pass rate drops with chain length and test-suite size (GPT-5.2 Chat PRD from >60% to ~10% in the largest test bin). F2P falls while P2P stays high as statefulness increases (Sonnet F2P about -30 pp Individual -> PRD; Gemini Flash Lite 52.45% -> 27.65%). With OpenHands, PRD and Global cost more per task than Individual (e.g. Sonnet $14.27 / $21.46 / $47.08); with Aider, Codex Mini costs about the same or less ($0.64 / $0.63 / $0.58) while Gemini 2.5 Flash costs more ($0.82 / $2.52 / $3.96). Agents show higher cognitive complexity and SQALE debt than human code (e.g. Gemini 3 Pro 7/7 Haystack PRs with debt surging in the final bin). Dominant failure mode in Global: 'Solving Previous Issues' 44.4% (20), then incorrect implementation 20.0% (9), out of budget 13.3% (6). No significance tests
